engineering_assessment.topic: Exact spec and existing collect-plan admission before CUDA
engineering_assessment.assessment: The tool first requires its stage, enabled spec, batch128, two updates, prefix8, minimum20000, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and exact working root. It hashes its own source and review, checks review stage/PASS/zero blockers/tool SHA, and requires canonical spec membership. Output must be absent. It hashes the exact collection plan and invokes that snapshot's existing load_plan before any model initialization. load_plan checks its admitted recipe, all98 source hashes, all7 input entries and the already bound successful FIT-smoke evidence. The capacity tool then requires the exact host/root/branch, non-smoke collect mode, round1 and shard0 of4.
engineering_assessment.invocation_boundary: The spec binds absolute command and task metadata. The tool itself checks CWD and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES; it does not read its native wrapper status or compare sys.argv/sys.executable with spec.command. This admission therefore covers only launching the listed command under the listed unique native task from the specified root with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=3, not arbitrary invocations of the tool.

engineering_assessment.topic: Real completed TRAIN-prefix reconstruction and input provenance
engineering_assessment.assessment: Selects manifest.train[::4][:8] from the exact hash-validated TRAIN manifest, requires published progress>=8 and checks all eight caches for sequence identity, embedded exact collect-plan hash and the entire expected valid noninitial stride-labelled frame list. Uses rebuild_state for the first128 available records in that deterministic prefix order and requires exactly128 finite states. It hashes the same cache bytes it parses. The collector publishes its sequence count after saving that whole cache, so later collection can continue without a full terminal receipt.
engineering_assessment.data_limits: The batch is the first128 labelled states across that prefix, not an equal per-sequence sample; some of the eight caches may contribute no state. It is reused for update2. Data provenance, crops, saved history and target follow the existing FIT helper; quality/gain labels are freshly recomputed. The actual images, caches, progress and128-state availability were not read remotely in this review. Existing image files are not individually hash-enumerated by this tool; the original sealed collection/data admission remains inherited.

engineering_assessment.topic: Freeze, loss, backward and optimizer parity with FIT
engineering_assessment.assessment: Uses the same load_completed_executor, configure_policy_refresh, centered16x16 Hann window and policy_refresh_loss as FIT. The inherited loader validates original P1A epoch20/step50000 completion and loads the round1 executor state strictly; it does not initialize from capacity updates or smoke weights. configure_policy_refresh freezes the entire model, enables only preview/quality/gain, and retains eval mode. AdamW uses preview LR1e-5, quality/gain LR1e-4 and weight_decay1e-4. Each of exactly two updates computes both-modality primary and all four counterfactual action targets under no_grad from the current preview, backpropagates the real combined policy loss, checks nonzero gradients in all three policy modules, clips norm to1, checks finite norm and steps AdamW.
engineering_assessment.freeze_verification: Checks all final state tensors finite and every preexisting non-policy state entry bit-equal after both updates. It does not hardcode a251-entry count. The archived P25 FIT POST_AUDIT records251 unchanged non-policy tensors; that historical count was read locally and is not a new actual capacity-run observation. The CPU small-model check additionally confirmed executor parameters have requires_grad=false/no gradients and each policy prefix changes.

engineering_assessment.topic: CPU resource gate and same-card measurement limits
engineering_assessment.assessment: Source import, canonical plan validation, seed/precision setup, reconstruction, collation and finite checks precede nvidia-smi. The actual execution checks GPU3 free memory>=20000MiB and snapshots compute-process metadata before load_completed_executor initializes CUDA. It uses one CPU torch thread, disables TF32 and cudnn benchmarking, synchronizes before/resetting peak tracking and after each update, and reports peak allocated/reserved, total device memory, pre-CUDA free memory/processes, two update durations, losses/norms, batch size and cache hashes.
resource_limits: No actual GPU state was queried in this review. The approximately2.3GiB existing collector is user-reported context, not independently measured here. The runtime free-memory check is the operative gate.

Free memory is a point-in-time observation, not a reservation or a proof B128 will fit. The co-resident collector can vary its memory use. OOM remains a possible measurement outcome; the source has no retry, smaller-batch fallback or collector kill/restart.

At the real FIT image shapes, batch128 templates and search alone occupy288MiB in float32, excluding history/target, model, optimizer, activations and allocator overhead. CPU sample collation temporarily duplicates this image batch. Prefix cache parsing and checkpoint/state copies add host-memory work.

Reported times start after reconstruction and host-to-device transfer and end after each update's CUDA synchronization. They include loss/backward, gradient checks, clipping and optimizer step, including first-step optimizer-state allocation. They exclude full loader/image throughput and checkpoint I/O. Nonzero-gradient checks are stricter than full non-smoke FIT's per-step path.

Existing GPU3 collector concurrency affects elapsed times. Peak torch allocated/reserved figures are for this process; they do not include the collector's allocations. No unconcurrent latency, full-loader throughput, epoch time, convergence or full-FIT batch recommendation is certified.

engineering_assessment.topic: Writes, collector isolation and result scope
engineering_assessment.assessment: Only writes the absent spec.output JSON after successful updates and freeze/finite checks, then prints it. No torch.save, checkpoint write, collector-state write, collector signaling, dataset mutation or fallback exists. Capacity-trained weights remain in the process and are discarded. The JSON binds finalized spec bytes, canonical spec digest and tool SHA and marks checkpoint_written/full_collection_acceptance/full_fit_admitted/benchmark_evidence false.
engineering_assessment.scope_limit: This is a separately admitted short capacity measurement. It does not replace the existing two-update FIT smoke, perform collection acceptance, persist usable weights, admit full FIT or round2, or provide benchmark evidence.
